newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to eliminate tariffs on 209 info items.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to eliminate tariffs on 209 info items.

text.p: Taiwan on Wednesday said it would eliminate tariffs on 201 information technology products by 2000, but eight other key items would have to wait until 2002.

"We have just completed talks with some 30 countries in late January in Geneva about the Information Technology Agreement," Hsu Lai-fa, a director of the Economics Ministry's Industrial Development Bureau, told Reuters.
He said the tariff cuts would begin on July 1, 1997, and would be carried out in four phases until tariffs on the 201 items were reduced to zero by January 1, 2000.
"But all sides agreed that we can postpone our zero tariff cuts on eight products to 2002," he said by telephone.
The eight items include mobile phones, telephone and telex switching machines and parts, fibre-optic cable, and digital video discs, Hsu said.
Hsu said the cuts on the eight items would be done in six phases until tariffs were reduced to zero by January 1, 2002.
Leaders of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum economies agreed last November to support a U.S. plan to scrap tariffs on trade in computers, memory chips and telecommunications equipment.
Washington had pressed for zero tariffs on information technology by a 2000 deadline.
"Overall, the plan will benefit Taiwan's industry as it will help our exports of information technology products," Hsu said.
But he said the tariff reductions would hurt the island's fledging telecommunications industry, prompting the government to postpone some of the cuts to reduce the impact.

Taiwan's computer hardware industry, the world's third-largest, grew 28.1 percent in 1996 to US$24.174 billion from 1995's $18.871 billion, the semi-official Institute for Information Industry said in a November forecast.
